contentEn: To trace hotel food and beverage ingredient loss, check four stages in order: purchasing, receiving, preparation, and the buffet counter. Find out which stage the loss really falls in, and only then decide whether staffing or processes need to change. There is one step before the four stages: first rule out distortions caused by how costs are recorded.

When the food cost percentage goes up, the usual reaction is to suspect the kitchen and then talk about replacing or cutting staff. Ingredients pass through several hands between the order and the guest's plate, and any of them can introduce an error; changing staff before the problem is located often just produces the same figures and a more tense kitchen. The executive chef understands yields better than anyone, so the chef should lead the checks and help set the standards.
## What should loss be compared against first?

The definition of food cost in the 11th Revised Edition of USALI (the Uniform System of Accounts for the Lodging Industry) states that spoilage, waste and spillage are included in Cost of Food Sales, while staff meals, food items transferred to other departments, and food used for gratis presentation to guests and third parties are not included and are charged to the appropriate accounts instead. So when the food cost percentage looks high, the first step is to check whether staff meals, food transferred to the bar or other departments, and complimentary food have been mixed in; food used by the banquet kitchen is part of food cost in any case and is not among the exclusions. If the basis is not clear, no amount of detailed checking in the four stages will make the figures reconcile. The 12th Revised Edition of USALI was published in July 2024 and has been effective since January 1, 2026, but its full text must be purchased and could not be read for this article, so the 11th Revised Edition is used as the basis.

Once the basis is right, find something to compare against. Part III, Financial Ratios and Operating Metrics, of the 11th Revised Edition of USALI explains that food cost percentage is used to evaluate whether a venue or the catering/banquet department has issues with portion size, waste, theft or other problems in controlling food costs, and that managers should compare actual cost percentages with budgeted or potential (theoretical) cost percentages; potential cost percentages take into account selling prices, purchasing costs and sales mix, and include the desired portion size and the expected waste. The gap between actual and potential is the part to look for in the four stages.

This gap shows how much money is unaccounted for, but not which stage it lies in or why. The same percentage point may come from one short-weight delivery, or from a dish that has been over-portioned for a long time. If opening and closing inventory are counted in different ways, the gap can also grow or shrink for no real reason, so stocktakes should be done at a fixed time, with a fixed method, by the storekeeper and finance together.
## In what order should the owner check?
Start with what to check at each of the four stages. The table is best agreed by finance and the executive chef together; the sections that follow explain each stage.
| Stage | What to check | Which records to use | Who verifies |
| Purchasing | Whether order quantities exceed forecast usage, and whether specifications are clearly written | Purchase orders, usage forecasts, inventory counts | Finance, executive chef |

| Receiving | Whether delivered weight, quantity and specifications match the purchase order | Purchase inspection records, weighing slips | Storekeeper or receiving clerk, not the person who placed the order |

| Preparation | Whether yields of the main ingredients and plated portions match the standard recipes | Yield test sheets, standard recipes | Led by the executive chef, with finance checking alongside |
| Buffet counter | How much buffet food and pre-prepared food is thrown away | Waste weighing records | Restaurant manager, executive chef |

There are two reasons for this order. Errors upstream carry downstream: suppose, hypothetically, that two kilograms were missing at receiving; no amount of saving in preparation can make that up. The first two stages mostly use existing documents and are the easiest to check; buffet waste is the most visible but needs separate weighing, so it comes last.
Who makes the call depends on how the hotel is operated.

At a managed hotel, day-to-day checks are carried out by the operator's food and beverage and finance managers. Before approving any staffing change, the owner can ask the operator to report, stage by stage, where the gap lies. Each side's approval authority is governed by the management agreement.

At a franchised hotel, first see whether the brand has standard recipes and purchasing specifications; if it does, use the brand standards as the basis for potential cost. If the owner operates the franchised hotel, the general manager leads; if a management company has been hired, treat it as a managed hotel.

At an unbranded, independent owner-operated hotel, standard recipes and yields have to be set in-house: the executive chef proposes them, the general manager and the owner confirm them, and they are put in writing as the benchmark for future comparisons.
## What should be checked at purchasing and receiving?

At purchasing, look at order quantities and specifications. When order quantities exceed forecast usage, the excess sits in the store until it expires and ends up in cost as spoilage; when specifications are vague, for example with no bone-in ratio or cut specified, the ingredients that arrive have low yields from the start. The evidence for this stage is purchase orders, usage forecasts and month-end stocktakes.

At receiving, check whether what arrived is what the purchase order specified. The law already requires this record. Article 53 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (a Chinese law) provides that food business enterprises must establish a food purchase inspection record system and truthfully record the name, specification, quantity and other details of the food; Article 55 requires food service providers to set and implement raw material control requirements. When checking for loss, look at the purchase inspection records together with actual weights: short weight, excessive ice glaze and wrong specifications all show up at this step. Separating the receiver from the person who places the order has been covered in an earlier article on this site about dividing purchasing duties, so it is not repeated here.
## How do you check hotel food and beverage ingredient loss at the preparation stage?

At the preparation stage, look at yield, which is the usable net weight after processing divided by the gross weight. The method is to pick a few high-cost main ingredients and, after each delivery, have the executive chef or a designated cook process them according to the standard recipe, weigh the gross and net amounts, record them on the yield test sheet, and compare the result with the yield in the standard recipe. Before testing, fix the trimming requirements and the point at which weighing takes place: weigh frozen products for gross weight only after thawing and draining, and trim the same cut to the same standard, so that results from different batches and different cooks can be compared. Plated portions are also checked at this stage: weigh a few finished dishes and see whether they match the recipe.

Work it through with a set of hypothetical figures. A main ingredient costs RMB 60 per kilogram gross; with a standard recipe yield of 70%, the net cost is about RMB 85.7 per kilogram. One batch tests at a yield of 60%, and the net cost becomes RMB 100 per kilogram. The gap shows up in the preparation records, but the cause may lie on either side: if the batch itself was substandard, for example with too much ice or undersized pieces, the problem is at receiving; if the ingredients were fine but over-trimmed, the problem is in preparation technique. Telling the two apart also takes tests on both sides: have a different cook test the same batch again and see whether the results are close; have the same cook process ingredients from two suppliers and see whether the gap follows the supplier. These figures only demonstrate the method and do not represent the actual yield of any ingredient.
## What is checked last, at the buffet counter?

At the buffet counter, record the weight of pre-prepared food and buffet food that is finally thrown away, convert it to cost, and see what share of the gap between actual and potential it accounts for. How to record the three kinds of leftovers (pre-prepared food, the buffet counter and guest plates) separately, and how to adjust replenishment, has been covered in an earlier article on this site about breakfast waste. The point to add here is the legal requirement. Article 7 of the Anti-Food Waste Law of the People's Republic of China (a Chinese law) requires catering service operators to establish and improve management systems for food purchasing, storage and processing; those providing buffet service must proactively inform consumers of the dining rules and food waste prevention requirements, provide tableware in different sizes, and remind consumers to take appropriate amounts.
## How do you run a small trial first, and when do you stop?

First choose three to five of the highest-cost ingredients and check them over one full stocktaking cycle: weigh every delivery, test the yield of every batch, weigh buffet waste every day, and at the end of the cycle compare the results against actual and potential food cost. Before the trial, finance and the executive chef should write down two criteria: how concentrated the gap must be in one stage to count as successfully located, and how large a weighing error counts as normal fluctuation. Set the values according to the precision of the hotel's scales and records, write them into the pilot record, and do not change them after the trial.

Adjust or stop in the following situations. If weighing and testing crowd into the service peak, reduce the number of items or move the work to off-peak hours; if the gap is spread across all stages and is not concentrated in any one, go back and recheck the stocktakes and the recording of transfers and staff meals; if there is any sign of storage being extended or food safety requirements being lowered to reduce waste, stop immediately. Only once the gap has been located should changes to specifications, suppliers, receiving or training be discussed; whether to change staffing comes last and must be based on the stage identified.
## What does this approach not cover?

The four-stage check shows where loss occurs; it does not replace theft investigations or internal audits, and it does not deal with menu pricing or menu mix. Whether food can still be used is always decided by food safety requirements. At hotels that serve breakfast only, run very small food and beverage operations, or receive their main ingredients processed and delivered by a central kitchen, there is limited room for in-house preparation, so in this article's judgment they can focus on the three stages of purchasing, receiving and the buffet counter, while keeping spot checks on plated portions and using the central kitchen's yields and delivery records as the basis for comparison. This article does not cover selling breakfast to non-residents or outsourcing the entire kitchen. MarvelBros C&T can help align the four-stage check with a hotel's food cost reports.

content: 酒店餐饮菜单精简，先砍高峰时段贡献低、专用原料又经常损耗的那一类菜。只占其中一项的菜另作处理：高峰贡献低但原料与其他菜共用的，可以先留着；高峰有人点但损耗高的，先改做法和备料，不急着撤。
菜单变长，常见的来路是一道道加上去的：品牌推新品，熟客点过一次，宴会要过一道菜。精简时最常见的做法，是把点得最少的几道划掉。点得少本身说明不了这道菜的去留，它是否在最忙的时候帮厨房赚钱，它的原料是否在库房里持续放坏，这两件事才决定先砍谁。
## 为什么不能只看销量和毛利？
常用的菜单分析方法叫菜单工程（英文直译）。康奈尔大学酒店管理学院教授基姆斯（Sheryl E. Kimes）2004年在该校酒店业研究中心的报告中描述过这种做法：逐道菜算出单位毛利（售价减成本）和销量，画在一张图上，按两项是否高于平均分成四类；报告建议把销量高的两类作为提价候选，并写到使用这种方法的餐厅通常每月复核一次。该报告在菜单工程这一节讨论的是定价。

本文判断，这两项指标看不到两件事。一是时间：全天销量相同的两道菜，一道集中在晚市高峰，一道散在下午，对厨房的意义完全不同。二是损耗：单位毛利通常按标准菜谱的原料成本算，放坏丢掉的那部分不在里面。USALI第12版于2024年7月出版、2026年1月1日起施行，其正文需购买，本文未能读到，故以第11版为据。USALI（英文名直译为住宿业统一会计制度）第11版写明，腐坏、浪费和洒漏计入食品成本。这些损耗落在餐厅的总食品成本里，分不到哪一道菜头上，所以要另外归一次。
## 业主先按哪张表分类？
先把菜分成四类。高低按本店同一菜单里同类菜的平均来分。这张表适合由行政总厨和财务一起填，后面几节说明两项怎么算。
| 类别 | 高峰贡献 | 损耗 | 怎么处理 |
| 先砍 | 低 | 高 | 停采专用原料，售完即撤 |
| 改做法 | 高 | 高 | 调整备料批量、份量或原料，再观察 |
| 暂留 | 低 | 低 | 不急着撤，下次复核再看 |
| 保留 | 高 | 低 | 不动，作为高峰主力 |
改做法这一类不急着撤，是因为它在高峰有人点，撤掉会直接少一块收入。可以先缩小每次备料的批量，把专用原料换成与其他菜共用的原料，或者增加小份。《中华人民共和国反食品浪费法》第七条要求餐饮服务经营者合理确定数量、分量，提供小份餐等不同规格选择；提供团体用餐服务的，要把防止食品浪费的理念纳入菜单设计。改完再观察一个周期，损耗降不下来，再归入先砍类。

谁来拍板，看经营方式。委托管理的酒店，菜单调整通常由管理方的餐饮负责人提出；业主在批准之前，可以要求看到这张分类表和每道拟撤菜的两项数据，审批权限以管理合同的约定为准。特许加盟的酒店，先查品牌有没有规定必须保留的核心菜品或招牌菜，这类菜要撤，须先取得品牌同意；业主自营的由总经理牵头，另聘管理公司的按委托管理处理。无品牌的业主自营酒店，没有外部菜单标准，由行政总厨提出、总经理和业主确认，并把分类结果和理由留底，下次复核时有据可比。
## 酒店餐饮菜单的高峰贡献怎么算？

高峰，指本店厨房或餐位最紧张的时段。各店不同，用收银系统按小时的点单量和出餐时间就能找出来。没有按小时记录的店，先用最忙的那个餐段代替，连续记几个星期，再逐步细到小时。高峰要按本店的瓶颈来定：厨房先满的，看出餐时间；餐位先满的，看翻台和等位。高峰贡献，是一道菜在高峰时段的销量乘以单位毛利。还要看它在高峰占用了多少关键工位的时间：一道菜要占炒锅或烤箱很久，高峰多出一份，可能就挤掉别的几份。占用时间可以在高峰时段按工位抽记几次出一份菜的起止时刻，看大致范围即可。
用一组假设数字推演。某个四周的盘点周期里，菜甲在高峰卖出12份，单位毛利40元，高峰贡献480元；它用一种专用原料，周期内这种原料被丢弃的金额是900元。菜乙在高峰卖出30份，单位毛利35元，高峰贡献1050元；它的原料都与其他菜共用，归到它名下的丢弃只有100元。按前面所说的同类均值来分，菜甲高峰贡献低、损耗高，属于先砍的一类；菜乙高峰贡献高、损耗低，应当保留。
两边都要再看一眼。菜甲如果在下午茶或夜宵时段卖得好，可以考虑只放进那个时段的菜单，不必全天撤掉；菜乙如果高峰出餐经常拖慢整桌上菜，高峰贡献要打折看。这组数字只演示算法，不代表任何菜品的实际毛利或损耗。
单位毛利用哪个数，要先统一。售价扣掉标准菜谱的原料成本，各道菜才能放在一起比；套餐和宴会里的菜没有单独售价，本文判断先排除在外，单点菜单分完类再看。
## 损耗怎么归到一道菜上？

先把原料分成两种。只有这道菜用的叫专用原料，几道菜都用的叫共用原料。专用原料的采购和丢弃，可以整笔归到这道菜；共用原料的丢弃很难拆到某道菜，本文判断不必硬拆，把它留在总损耗里即可。专用原料多、销量又低的菜，周转慢、容易放过期，是损耗最集中的地方。鲜活和保质期短的专用原料最要紧；冻品周转慢，放坏的少，主要占的是库存资金和冷库位置。还有一种容易漏掉：为了高峰出得快提前备好的半成品，卖不完到时限就丢，这部分也要按专用原料归到对应的菜。
丢弃金额从哪里来，取决于本店有没有逐环记录损耗。怎样按采购、验收、切配、餐台定位损耗，另有专文讨论，这里只需要专用原料的采购量、丢弃量和月末盘点三份数字。
## 砍之前先查哪些承诺，按什么顺序撤？
撤菜之前，先查三类承诺：品牌标准要求保留的菜，已经卖出的套餐、宴会菜单和协议里写明的菜，为素食、过敏等饮食需要保留的选择。前两类撤之前要先处理合同或取得同意，最后一类即使数量少也要留出替代。
撤的顺序也有讲究。先停止采购专用原料，把库存用完，菜单上标注售完即止；库存用完再从纸质菜单、线上点餐和预订平台上同步撤下。直接划掉而不管库存，剩下的专用原料就成了新的损耗。
## 怎样先试，什么时候收手？
先在一个餐厅或一个出品区试一个完整的盘点周期。试之前，行政总厨、餐厅经理和财务先写下判定标准和收手条件，例如专用原料的丢弃金额下降多少算有效，高峰的桌均消费和出餐时间波动多大以内算正常。具体数值按本店前几个周期的记录定，写进试行记录，试完不再改。两项指标各有局限：丢弃金额下降，能说明专用原料少丢了，说明不了客人是否满意；桌均消费会随客源结构和节假日变化，要和同期的客源构成放在一起看。
出现下列情况，就恢复被撤的菜或停止扩大：客人点名要这道菜、评价里反复提到；高峰桌均消费的下降超出事先写定的范围；协议客户或宴会客户提出必须保留。结果站得住，再按同样顺序处理下一批先砍类的菜。
## 这套方法管不到什么？
它只决定先砍哪一类，不决定菜单该留多少道，也不处理定价和新菜开发。餐位和厨房常年都坐不满、忙不满的餐厅，高峰与平时差别不大，本文判断可以用全天贡献代替高峰贡献，损耗一项照算。自助早餐的品种增减，本站讨论早餐浪费的旧文另有讨论；损耗发生在哪一环，要按专文的方法逐环查。本文不涉及厨房整体外包。食物能否继续使用，一律按食品安全要求处理。迈创兄弟C&T可以协助把菜单分类和食品成本报表对齐。

contentEn: When trimming a hotel food and beverage menu, cut first the category of dishes with low peak-period contribution whose dedicated ingredients are often wasted. Dishes that meet only one of these conditions are handled differently: those with low peak contribution but ingredients shared with other dishes can stay for now; those that sell at peak but have high waste should first have their recipe and prep changed, with no rush to remove them.

Menus usually grow long one dish at a time: the brand launches a new item, a regular orders something once, a banquet asks for a dish. The most common way to trim is to cross off the few dishes that sell least. Selling little does not in itself decide whether a dish stays or goes; what decides which dishes go first is whether a dish earns money for the kitchen at its busiest times, and whether its ingredients keep spoiling in the store.
## Why can't you look only at sales volume and gross profit?

The common method of menu analysis is called menu engineering. Sheryl E. Kimes, a professor at the Cornell University School of Hotel Administration, described this approach in a 2004 report for the university's Center for Hospitality Research: calculate the contribution margin (selling price less the cost) and the number sold for each dish, plot them on a graph, and divide the dishes into four categories according to whether each figure is above average; the report suggests treating the two high-volume categories as candidates for price increases, and notes that restaurants using the method generally review the results every month. In its menu engineering section, the report discusses pricing.

This article's judgment is that these two measures miss two things. The first is timing: two dishes with the same daily sales, one concentrated at the dinner peak and the other spread across the afternoon, mean completely different things to the kitchen. The second is waste: the unit contribution margin is usually based on the ingredient cost in the standard recipe, and the portion that spoils and is thrown away is not included. The 12th Revised Edition of USALI (the Uniform System of Accounts for the Lodging Industry) was published in July 2024 and has been effective since January 1, 2026, but its full text must be purchased and could not be read for this article, so the 11th Revised Edition is used as the basis. The 11th Revised Edition of USALI states that spoilage, waste and spillage are included in Cost of Food Sales. This waste lands in the restaurant's total food cost and cannot be assigned to any one dish, so it has to be attributed separately.
## Which table should the owner use to classify dishes?

First divide the dishes into four categories. High and low are judged against the average for similar dishes on the same menu at the hotel. The table is best filled in by the executive chef and finance together; the sections that follow explain how the two measures are calculated.
| Category | Peak contribution | Waste | What to do |
| Cut first | Low | High | Stop buying dedicated ingredients; remove once sold out |
| Change the method | High | High | Adjust prep batch sizes, portions or ingredients, then observe |
| Keep for now | Low | Low | No rush to remove; look again at the next review |
| Keep | High | Low | Leave unchanged as a peak mainstay |

Dishes in the change-the-method category are not removed in a hurry because they sell at peak, and removing them would cut revenue directly. You can first reduce the size of each prep batch, replace dedicated ingredients with ones shared with other dishes, or add smaller portions. Article 7 of the Anti-Food Waste Law of the People's Republic of China (a Chinese law) requires catering service operators to set quantities and portion sizes reasonably and to offer choices of different sizes such as small portions; those providing group dining services must build the idea of preventing food waste into menu design. After the change, observe for another cycle; if waste does not come down, move the dish into the cut-first category.

Who makes the call depends on how the hotel is operated. At a managed hotel, menu changes are usually proposed by the operator's food and beverage manager; before approving, the owner can ask to see this classification table and the two measures for each dish proposed for removal, and approval authority is governed by the management agreement. At a franchised hotel, first check whether the brand requires certain core dishes or signature dishes to be kept; removing any of these requires the brand's consent first. If the owner operates the franchised hotel, the general manager leads; if a management company has been hired, treat it as a managed hotel. At an unbranded owner-operated hotel there is no external menu standard: the executive chef proposes, the general manager and the owner confirm, and the classification results and reasons are kept on file so that the next review has a basis for comparison.
## How do you calculate peak contribution for a hotel food and beverage menu?

Peak means the period when the hotel's kitchen or seating is under the most pressure. It differs from hotel to hotel and can be identified from hourly order counts and ticket times in the point-of-sale (POS) system. A hotel without hourly records can start by using its busiest meal period instead, record it for several weeks in a row, and then gradually narrow it down to the hour. The peak should be defined by the hotel's bottleneck: if the kitchen fills up first, look at ticket times; if seating fills up first, look at table turns and waiting. Peak contribution is a dish's sales during the peak multiplied by its unit contribution margin. Also look at how much time it ties up at key stations during the peak: if a dish occupies a wok or an oven for a long time, one extra portion at peak may push out several others. To gauge the time tied up, sample a few plates at each station during the peak, recording the start and finish times of each; a rough range is enough.

Work it through with a set of hypothetical figures. In a four-week stocktaking cycle, Dish A sells 12 portions at peak with a unit contribution margin of RMB 40, for a peak contribution of RMB 480; it uses one dedicated ingredient, and RMB 900 worth of that ingredient is thrown away during the cycle. Dish B sells 30 portions at peak with a unit contribution margin of RMB 35, for a peak contribution of RMB 1,050; all its ingredients are shared with other dishes, and only RMB 100 of waste is attributed to it. Classified by the average for similar dishes described earlier, Dish A has low peak contribution and high waste, so it belongs in the cut-first category; Dish B has high peak contribution and low waste and should be kept.

Both sides deserve a second look. If Dish A sells well at afternoon tea or late-night supper, consider putting it only on that period's menu rather than removing it all day; if Dish B often holds up the delivery of a whole table's dishes at peak, its peak contribution should be discounted. These figures only demonstrate the method and do not represent the actual margin or waste of any dish.

First agree which figure to use for the unit contribution margin. Only when it is the selling price minus the standard recipe ingredient cost can dishes be compared with one another; dishes in set menus and banquets have no separate selling price, so this article's judgment is to leave them out at first and look at them after the a la carte menu has been classified.
## How is waste attributed to a single dish?

First divide ingredients into two kinds. Ingredients used by only one dish are dedicated ingredients; those used by several dishes are shared ingredients. Purchases and waste of dedicated ingredients can be attributed in full to that dish; waste of shared ingredients is hard to split among dishes, and this article's judgment is that it need not be forced apart and can stay in total waste. Dishes with many dedicated ingredients and low sales turn over slowly and easily pass their expiry dates, which is where waste is most concentrated. Fresh, live and short-shelf-life dedicated ingredients matter most; frozen products turn over slowly and spoil less, and mainly tie up inventory funds and cold storage space. One more kind is easily missed: semi-finished items prepared in advance so that the peak runs faster, which are thrown away when unsold at their time limit; these too should be attributed to the corresponding dishes as dedicated ingredients.

Where the waste figures come from depends on whether the hotel records waste stage by stage. How to locate waste across purchasing, receiving, preparation and the buffet counter is covered in a separate article; here, only three figures for dedicated ingredients are needed: purchase quantities, waste quantities and month-end stocktakes.
## Before cutting, which commitments should be checked, and in what order should dishes be removed?

Before removing a dish, check three kinds of commitments: dishes the brand standards require to be kept; dishes written into set menus, banquet menus and agreements already sold; and options kept for vegetarian, allergy and other dietary needs. For the first two, contracts must be dealt with or consent obtained before removal; for the last, an alternative must be kept even if numbers are small.

The order of removal also matters. First stop buying the dedicated ingredients, use up the stock, and mark the dish on the menu as available while stocks last; once the stock is used up, remove it at the same time from printed menus, online ordering and booking platforms. Crossing a dish off without dealing with its stock turns the remaining dedicated ingredients into new waste.
## How do you trial it first, and when do you stop?

First trial it in one restaurant or one production area for a full stocktaking cycle. Before the trial, the executive chef, the restaurant manager and finance should write down the success criteria and stop conditions, for example how far waste spending on dedicated ingredients must fall to count as effective, and how much fluctuation in peak average spend per table and ticket times counts as normal. Set the specific values from the hotel's records for previous cycles, write them into the trial record, and do not change them after the trial. Each measure has its limits: a fall in waste spending shows that less of the dedicated ingredients was thrown away, but not whether guests are satisfied; average spend per table varies with the guest mix and holidays, so it should be read alongside the guest mix for the same period.

In any of the following cases, restore the removed dish or stop extending the change: guests ask for the dish by name, or reviews mention it repeatedly; the fall in peak average spend per table goes beyond the range written down in advance; or contract clients or banquet clients insist that it be kept. If the results hold up, handle the next batch of cut-first dishes in the same order.
## What does this method not cover?

It decides only which category goes first, not how many dishes the menu should keep, and it does not deal with pricing or new dish development. In restaurants whose seats and kitchen are never full at any time of year, there is little difference between peak and normal times, and this article's judgment is that whole-day contribution can be used in place of peak contribution, while waste is still calculated as before. Adding or removing items on the breakfast buffet is discussed in an earlier article on this site about breakfast waste; which stage waste occurs in should be checked stage by stage using the method in the separate article. This article does not cover outsourcing the entire kitchen. Whether food can still be used is always decided by food safety requirements. content: 酒店餐饮外包以后，业主每月只看一张合并的月度核对表，把出品、停售、客诉、结算四项放在一起，按同一套口径决定约谈、扣减和续约：涉及食品安全的偏离出现一次就约谈；其他偏离本月和上月都出现才约谈；扣减只按合同已经写明的条款，以月表记录为凭；续不续约，看全年的月表。
餐厅或厨房交给第三方经营以后，很多酒店每月只收到一笔租金或分成，再看到几条差评。四项分散在前厅、财务和承包方手里，没有人把它们放在一起看，问题容易拖到续约前才集中暴露。本文讨论的是合同签订以后、履约期间每月怎样核对，不讨论合同怎么签。
## 为什么外包以后还要每月核对？

USALI第12版于2024年7月出版、2026年1月1日起施行，其正文需购买，本文未能读到，故以第11版为据。USALI（英文名直译为住宿业统一会计制度，下称统一会计制度）第11版把租用酒店场地的商户支付的款项，列在杂项收入的场地出租与特许经营收入（英文直译）里。第五部分说明，一项收入按总额还是净额记账，要看酒店在交易中是主要责任方还是代理方，并把客人认为由酒店负责提供、包括不满意时由酒店补救，列为按总额记账的一项强指标。
本文判断，这两点对业主有两层意思。按净额记账时，酒店账上只剩收到的租金或分成，餐厅的营业额和成本不在酒店的餐饮部门里，要核分成，就得另外取得承包方的营业数据。另一层是，客人未必知道餐厅由谁经营，吃得不好，评价落在酒店名下。

法规要求许可证和健康证明有效，健康检查按年进行。《中华人民共和国食品安全法》第三十五条规定，从事餐饮服务应当依法取得许可；第四十五条要求接触直接入口食品的从业人员每年进行健康检查，取得健康证明后方可上岗；第一百二十二条第二款规定，明知对方未取得食品生产经营许可仍为其提供生产经营场所的，要承担相应法律责任，使消费者受到损害的还要承担连带责任。承包方的许可证和员工健康证明是否在有效期内，适合每月核一次。
## 这张月度核对表查哪四项？
先看表。偏离，指与合同、品牌标准或双方书面确认的口径不一致；许可证和健康证明的问题按食品安全类处理。四行的处理方式与首段的判定口径相同。
| 项目 | 每月核对什么 | 用哪份记录 | 偏离时怎么处理 |
| 出品 | 抽查菜品的份量、温度和出餐时间，许可证和健康证明是否有效 | 值班经理抽查记录，承包方证照复印件 | 证照或食品安全问题一次即约谈，其他本月和上月都偏离才约谈 |
| 停售 | 约定营业时段内的停售和提前收档，住客早餐与送餐是否按约提供 | 前厅交接记录，承包方停售登记，收银分时数据 | 本月和上月都偏离才约谈，属合同扣减条款的按条款扣减 |
| 客诉 | 涉及餐饮的投诉和评价，按食品安全、服务、价格分类，是否按约定时限结案 | 前厅投诉记录，在线评价，承包方处理单 | 食品安全类一次即约谈，其他本月和上月都偏离才约谈 |
| 结算 | 申报营业额与收银流水、挂房账核对，分成、代收款和能耗分摊 | 收银系统导出，挂房账明细，分表读数 | 少付部分当月按合同追收，无法说明的差额本月和上月都出现才约谈 |
表由谁填，要事先分好。出品由值班经理或质检人员抽查，停售和客诉由前厅汇总，结算由财务核对，承包方的店长在月表上签字确认，有异议的写明理由。四项只占一页，月初第一周内交到业主或总经理手里。

出品抽查要让结果能前后比较：每月换不同餐段，不提前通知，抽查的菜品和记录方式保持一致。客诉一行先按食品安全、服务、价格分开，再看是否在约定时限内结案；同一类问题反复出现，比单月条数多少更值得关注。业主读这张表，先看有没有食品安全类记录，再看哪一项本月和上月都偏离，最后看结算有没有追收事项，三步就能决定本月要不要约谈。续约前，把全年的月表按四项排开，看偏离是集中在少数月份还是一直存在、约谈以后有没有改善，再决定续约、续约时改条件还是到期更换。
## 酒店餐饮外包的结算怎么核？
结算这一行最容易只看一个数。分成按承包方申报的营业额计算时，要把申报额和酒店能看到的数据对一遍：收银系统的流水，住客挂在房账上的餐饮消费，酒店代收后转付承包方的款项，以及水电燃气的分表读数和分摊。
用一组假设数字推演。某月承包方申报营业额30万元，酒店从收银系统导出的同期流水是31.2万元，差1.2万元；合同约定的分成比例假设为10%，按申报额计算，分成少了1200元。
差额要先找原因，再下结论。其中0.8万元如果是月底挂房账跨月入账，属于时点差，下月会对上；剩下0.4万元如果找不到退单、团购核销或其他记录说明，才算本月结算项偏离。确认少付的部分，当月按合同追收。上月结算没有无法说明的差额，本月就记下偏离、请承包方书面说明，下月再看；上月也有，就约谈。
停售也要两边看。假设本月记录了三次晚市停售，其中一次是酒店自己安排燃气检修，这一次不能算在承包方头上；剩下两次是否构成偏离，看双方事先确认的口径。反过来，承包方没有登记、由前厅从住客投诉里发现的停售，要补进记录。这组数字只演示核对方法，不代表任何酒店的营业额、分成比例或差额水平。
## 三种经营方式下谁看这张表？
委托管理的酒店，承包方可能由管理方代业主选择和管理，也可能由业主直接签约。业主可以要求把这张月表附在每月的业主报告里，约谈由管理方执行；续约和更换承包方的审批权限，以管理合同的约定为准。
特许加盟的酒店，加盟合同是酒店与品牌签的，承包方不在其中。本文判断，早餐、送餐这类品牌要求的服务停了，品牌找的是酒店，所以停售一行要对照品牌标准核。外包合同由业主签，月表由总经理汇总、业主决定约谈和续约；另聘管理公司的，按委托管理处理。
业主自营的酒店，包括无品牌的单体酒店，由总经理汇总、财务核对结算、业主拍板。没有品牌标准可依，双方书面确认的服务口径就是这张表唯一的依据，要和月表放在一起留存。
## 怎样先试，什么时候收手？
先试一个季度。试之前，酒店和承包方把每项的口径书面确认：停售怎样算一次，出品抽查哪些菜、怎样记录，申报营业额从哪个系统取数。试行期间的月表只作约谈依据，不作扣减依据，让双方先把口径磨合清楚。
出现下列情况，就停下调整：某一项的数据连续拿不到，例如承包方的收银数据无法导出，先停评这一项、解决取数，不拿估算顶替；争议主要集中在口径理解上，先改口径，再恢复使用；任何食品安全问题，不等月表，当场按法规和酒店的应急程序处理。
每项指标都有局限。客诉条数会随入住率起落，要和当月住客人数一起看；出品抽查样本小，只能发现明显偏差；结算核对只能核到有记录的交易，现金收款如果不进收银系统，表上看不出来。本文判断，这张表适合发现问题、留下证据，判断责任还要结合原始记录。
## 这张表管不到什么？
它不讨论外包合同怎么签，也不判断餐饮该不该外包；外包与否属于餐段层面的判断，本站讨论餐饮营收的旧文另有分析。原料损耗出在哪一环，另有专文；逐批到货的验收，本站讨论布草外包验收的旧文另有做法。承包方与酒店之间的法律责任怎样划分，要看合同并听取律师意见。迈创兄弟C&T可以协助把这张月表和酒店现有报表接起来。

contentEn: After hotel food and beverage is outsourced, the owner reviews just one combined monthly review table each month, puts four items together, namely food quality, service stoppages, complaints and settlement, and uses one set of criteria to decide on formal talks, deductions and renewal: a deviation involving food safety triggers a formal talk with the operator the first time it occurs; any other deviation triggers a formal talk only if it occurs in both this month and last month; deductions follow only clauses already written into the contract, with the monthly table records as evidence; whether to renew depends on the monthly tables for the whole year.

After a restaurant or kitchen is handed to a third party to operate, many hotels receive only a rent payment or a revenue share each month, and then see a few negative reviews. The four items are scattered among the front office, finance and the operator, no one looks at them together, and problems tend to surface all at once only just before renewal. This article discusses how to check performance each month after the contract is signed, during the term of the contract; it does not discuss how the contract should be signed.
## Why check every month even after outsourcing?

The 12th Revised Edition of USALI was published in July 2024 and has been effective since January 1, 2026, but its full text must be purchased and could not be read for this article, so the 11th Revised Edition is used as the basis. The 11th Revised Edition of USALI (Uniform System of Accounts for the Lodging Industry) places the amounts paid by tenants who rent space in the hotel under Space Rental and Concessions within Miscellaneous Income. Part V explains that whether a revenue item is reported gross or net depends on whether the hotel is acting as a principal or as an agent in the transaction, and lists the customer's perspective that the hotel is responsible for providing the product or service, including remedies if the customer is dissatisfied, as a strong indicator for gross reporting.

This article's judgment is that these two points mean two things for the owner. Under net reporting, only the rent or revenue share received remains on the hotel's books, and the restaurant's revenue and costs are not in the hotel's food and beverage department; to check the revenue share, the owner has to obtain the operator's sales data separately. The other is that guests may not know who runs the restaurant; if the food is poor, the review lands under the hotel's name.

The regulations require the license and health certificates to be valid, with health checks carried out annually. Article 35 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (a Chinese law) provides that anyone engaged in catering services shall obtain a license in accordance with the law; Article 45 requires staff who handle ready-to-eat food to undergo a health examination every year and to start work only after obtaining a health certificate; Paragraph 2 of Article 122 provides that anyone who, while knowing that the other party has not obtained a food production or business license, still provides it with production or business premises shall bear the corresponding legal liability, and shall also bear joint and several liability if consumers are harmed. Whether the operator's license and its staff's health certificates are within their validity periods is suitable for checking once a month.
## Which four items does this monthly review table check?

Look at the table first. A deviation means anything inconsistent with the contract, brand standards or criteria both parties have confirmed in writing; problems with licenses and health certificates are handled as food safety matters. The handling in the four rows follows the same criteria as the first paragraph.
| Item | What to check each month | Which record to use | What to do on a deviation |

| Food quality | Spot-check portion size, temperature and serving time of dishes, and whether licenses and health certificates are valid | Duty manager spot-check records, copies of the operator's licenses and certificates | A license, certificate or food safety problem triggers a formal talk the first time; other deviations trigger one only if they occur in both this month and last month |

| Service stoppages | Stoppages and early closing within the agreed operating hours, and whether guest breakfast and room service are provided as agreed | Front office handover records, the operator's stoppage log, hourly cashier data | A formal talk only if deviations occur in both this month and last month; where a contract deduction clause applies, deduct under that clause |

| Complaints | Food and beverage complaints and reviews, classified as food safety, service or price, and whether they are closed within the agreed time limit | Front office complaint records, online reviews, the operator's handling forms | Food safety items trigger a formal talk the first time; others only if deviations occur in both this month and last month |

| Settlement | Declared revenue checked against cashier transaction records and charges posted to guest rooms; revenue share, amounts collected on the operator's behalf and energy cost allocation | Cashier system exports, room charge details, sub-meter readings | Any underpayment is recovered under the contract in the same month; an unexplained difference triggers a formal talk only if it appears in both this month and last month |

Who fills in the table should be decided in advance. Food quality is spot-checked by the duty manager or quality inspection staff, service stoppages and complaints are compiled by the front office, settlement is checked by finance, and the operator's store manager signs the monthly table to confirm it, writing down the reasons for any objection. The four items take up only one page and are delivered to the owner or the general manager within the first week of each month.

Food quality spot checks should produce results that can be compared over time: use a different meal period each month, give no advance notice, and keep the dishes checked and the recording method the same. In the complaints row, first separate food safety, service and price, then see whether cases are closed within the agreed time limit; the same type of problem recurring deserves more attention than the number of complaints in a single month. When reading this table, the owner first looks for any food safety records, then for any item that deviated in both this month and last month, and finally for any settlement recovery items; these three steps are enough to decide whether to hold a formal talk this month. Before renewal, lay out the full year of monthly tables by the four items, see whether deviations are concentrated in a few months or persist throughout, and whether things improved after formal talks, then decide whether to renew, renew on changed terms, or replace the operator when the contract expires.
## How do you check settlement for outsourced hotel food and beverage?

The settlement row is the easiest place to look at only one number. When the revenue share is calculated on revenue declared by the operator, check the declared amount against the data the hotel can see: cashier system transaction records, food and beverage spending that guests charge to their rooms, payments the hotel collects and passes on to the operator, and sub-meter readings and allocations for water, electricity and gas.

Work through a set of hypothetical figures. In one month the operator declares revenue of RMB 300,000, while the transaction records the hotel exports from the cashier system for the same period show RMB 312,000, a difference of RMB 12,000; assuming the contracted revenue share is 10%, calculating on the declared amount leaves the revenue share RMB 1,200 short.

Find the cause of a difference before drawing a conclusion. If RMB 8,000 of it comes from month-end room charges posted in the following month, it is a timing difference and will reconcile next month; only if the remaining RMB 4,000 cannot be explained by refunds, group-buying voucher redemptions or other records does it count as a deviation in this month's settlement item. Any confirmed underpayment is recovered under the contract in the same month. If last month's settlement had no unexplained difference, record the deviation this month, ask the operator for a written explanation, and look again next month; if last month also had one, hold a formal talk.

Service stoppages also need to be viewed from both sides. Suppose three dinner service stoppages are recorded this month, one of which was gas maintenance the hotel itself scheduled; that one cannot be counted against the operator. Whether the remaining two are deviations depends on the criteria both parties confirmed in advance. Conversely, stoppages the operator did not log and the front office discovered from guest complaints should be added to the records. These figures only demonstrate the checking method and do not represent any hotel's revenue, revenue share percentage or level of difference.
## Under the three operating models, who reviews this table?

In a hotel under a management contract, the operator may be selected and managed by the management company on the owner's behalf, or contracted directly by the owner. The owner can ask for this monthly table to be attached to each monthly owner's report, with formal talks carried out by the management company; approval authority for renewing or replacing the operator is as agreed in the management contract.

In a franchised hotel, the franchise agreement is between the hotel and the brand, and the operator is not a party to it. This article's judgment is that if brand-required services such as breakfast or room service stop, the brand holds the hotel responsible, so the service stoppages row should be checked against brand standards. The outsourcing contract is signed by the owner; the general manager compiles the monthly table, and the owner decides on formal talks and renewal. Where a management company is also engaged, treat it as a management contract.

In an owner-operated hotel, including an unbranded independent hotel, the general manager compiles the table, finance checks settlement, and the owner makes the final call. With no brand standards to rely on, the service criteria confirmed in writing by both parties are the only basis for this table and should be kept together with the monthly tables.
## How do you trial it first, and when do you stop?

Trial it for one quarter first. Before the trial, the hotel and the operator confirm the criteria for each item in writing: what counts as one stoppage, which dishes the food quality spot checks cover and how they are recorded, and which system declared revenue is taken from. During the trial, the monthly tables serve only as a basis for formal talks, not for deductions, so that both parties can first work out the criteria.

Stop and adjust when any of the following occurs: data for an item cannot be obtained month after month, for example the operator's cashier data cannot be exported, in which case first suspend scoring that item and fix the data access, without substituting estimates; disputes center mainly on how the criteria are understood, in which case first revise the criteria and then resume use; any food safety problem, which is handled on the spot under the law and the hotel's emergency procedures, without waiting for the monthly table.

Every indicator has limits. Complaint counts rise and fall with occupancy and should be read alongside the number of in-house guests that month; food quality spot checks have small samples and can only catch obvious deviations; settlement checks can only cover recorded transactions, and if cash receipts do not go into the cashier system, the table will not show them. This article's judgment is that this table is suited to finding problems and keeping evidence; determining responsibility also requires the original records.
